files.DEVELOPER_API.md:
# AC Shadows domain API 0.1.0

Package `saverift.ac-shadows`; extension API `acshadows.inventory`.
Runtime `isolated-js-v1`. One primary serializer. No ambient network/filesystem,
native DLL, account transport, host-specific UI page or parallel application.

## Queries

- `acshadows.inspect`: format, source SHA256, counts, capabilities, limits.
- `acshadows.inventory.list`: `offset`, `limit` (1–50), `search` (at most 200
  characters). Returns bounded inventory records with exact IDs, owner, current
  values and eligible fields. Only the named query methods are accepted.

Source hashes refer to the selected **main artifact**, including the wrapper for
native files. A `recordId` is valid only for that source and must not be reused
after a game save reorders/recreates records. Private key material is never a
query value. Native field witnesses are evidence, not arbitrary-write controls.

## Operations

`acshadows.inventory.setLevel` parameters:

```json
{"recordId":"source-bound record returned by query","expectedLevel":62,"level":61,"sourceSha256":"64 lowercase hexadecimal characters"}
```

`acshadows.inventory.setQuantity` parameters:

```json
{"recordId":"source-bound record returned by query","expectedQuantity":20,"quantity":21,"sourceSha256":"64 lowercase hexadecimal characters"}
```

Both use `apiVersion: "0.1.0"`, ordered write domain `inventory`; max 16
operations per plan. Exact schemas are in `manifest.json`. Additional properties,
unknown operations, invalid source/record/precondition, read-only fields,
duplicate field writes and out-of-range values fail closed. The custom UI
replaces an existing draft edit for the same record/field while retaining others.

Draft changes use the SDK CAS revision and subscription APIs. Stale revisions
reject. The UI stages requests; the trusted host compiles the draft and validates
the source and execution lock before preparing a candidate. UI code cannot
approve a candidate or publish it.

## Binary inputs and outputs

Native: one `main` file, one private 16-byte `ac-key`, optional `sibling` files.
Context: one `progression` (or `main`) file, optional siblings. All use opaque
binary artifact handles. `ac-key` is an input-only role declared in the manifest;
it must be supplied again to reopen a native candidate and must never be offered
as a result download. Actual main logical path is retained.

Candidate metadata binds source bundle digest, execution lock and operation
digest. The change report names resolved field offsets/before/after values and
explicitly reports `gameAcceptance: "not_run"`. The candidate validator checks
emitted binary artifacts, not only the in-memory planning buffer. Fresh-engine
reopen is a separate workbench phase. Context output never claims native-game
file status.

## Resources and unsupported inputs

Use default runner limits. Unknown native versions or non-stored target blocks
fail; a package must not inherit a Crimson trusted profile. No automated
production/registry action is part of this API. Optional local preparation is a
source utility, not a callable sandbox escape or new host primitive.
files.FORMAT_SUPPORT.md:
# Format, compatibility and evidence

| Input / domain | Support | Evidence and limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Windows PC outer wrapper + native container v54, prepared progression context at index 12 | Implemented | 40-byte wrapper retained; one selected 16-byte private transform key; target blocks must be flag 0; default 8 MiB per artifact applies |
| Extracted `AssassinProgressionSaveData` context | Implemented | Complete typed-property traversal; outputs remain extracted contexts |
| Untouched Oodle-compressed progression context | Rejected | `AC_OODLE_REQUIRED`; explicit local preparation required |
| Unknown native version, compression info, root, field type or truncated layout | Rejected | No guessed fallback offsets or opaque inventory skips |
| Xbox / PlayStation | Unsupported | No interchangeable-format claim, console title ID, transport or account grant |
| Existing Naoe/Yasuke gear level, 1–100 | Typed edit | Existing singleton gear with a positive level; exact record/precondition/source witnesses |
| Existing Naoe/Yasuke inventory stack, 1–999999 | Typed edit | Already-stacked level-zero entries only; no insertion or ownership change |
| Other owner profiles; singleton level-zero records | Read-only | Insufficient item-category evidence for safe edits |
| Player level, XP, prestige/mastery, skills, loadouts, engravings, item addition | Unsupported in this release | Prior research does not automatically qualify a new isolated operation |
| Localized catalog/art/stat calculator | Not bundled | Internal settings and instance IDs remain visible; no private data-provider reuse |

## Recovered structural facts

These rules derive from the existing AC research implementation, checked against
the selected authorized native fixture. They are not a new generic schema guess.

| Layer | Rule |
|---|---|
| Outer file | 40-byte header; first little-endian u64 is 36. Preserve all 40 bytes. Remaining bytes use a repeating 16-byte XOR transformation; rotate the base key by payload length modulo 16. This is obfuscation, not authentication. |
| Decoded header | u32 signature `0x00fedbac`, version 54, next word 4. The word at offset 12 is **not** the context count. Parse bounded framing to the footer. |
| Payload integrity | Seeded IEEE CRC32 (`0xF4C3B8A2`) stored at offset 16 over `[20, length-4)`. |
| Footer integrity | Seeded CRC32C/Castagnoli, reflected polynomial `0x82F63B78`, same seed, over `[0, length-4)`, stored in the final four bytes. Recompute after the payload CRC. |
| Context | 8-byte resource key, u32 record length, u32 plaintext length, magic `0x1004fa9957fbaa33`, seven compression-info bytes `03 00 05 00 00 04 00`, then bounded blocks. Record length includes the uncompressed-size field. |
| Block | Flag 0: u32 size followed by stored bytes. Flag 1: packed size, plain size, Adler32 seed 0 over packed data, then data. Maximum block size 262144. |
| Compression naming | Prior extraction labels the algorithm `OODLEMERMAIDOPTIMAL3`; inspected compressed block headers start `8c06`. Treat the decoder identity as external evidence, not a reason to embed a guessed Mermaid implementation. |
| Inventory root | `AssassinProgressionSaveData`, type hash 1868920887. Nested typed lengths/arrays/properties fully consumed. Exact IDs are decimal strings; never coerce 64-bit settings IDs to floating-point numbers. |
| Edits | Four-byte unsigned little-endian quantity/level writes at structurally resolved property offsets. No record regeneration or identifier allocation. |
| Preservation | Same-width native edits require only intended field bytes and two integrity words to change in decoded data. Wrapper, ordering, other contexts, unknown bytes and selected siblings stay identical. |

Selected baseline: native file 901,776 bytes, 61 contexts, 108 compressed blocks,
19,039,487 total plaintext bytes. Inventory context: 6,819,042 bytes,
86,929 objects, 193,505 fields, 2,174 inventory records. The local prepared
container is 7,459,585 bytes. Counts describe this fixture, not a version rule.

The key is selected private data, never an inferred user credential or public
constant. `inputOnlyRoles: ["ac-key"]` excludes it from candidate artifacts and
downloads. Additional selected sibling artifacts are returned unchanged. The
fixture contains a self-contained PC save; no assumption about a mandatory
console sibling set is made.

## Validation boundary

Prepared-file no-op is byte-identical to the **prepared selected input**. Local
preparation intentionally changes compression representation and container
integrity; its independent test must show identical plaintext in **all** contexts
relative to the original raw input. Do not call that conversion byte-identical.

The isolated connector validates container structure, both seeded CRCs, packed
block Adler values, and the entire editable progression tree. It preserves other
compressed contexts without claiming to understand their semantic fields. An
external independent oracle decompresses every original/candidate context and
checks exact plaintext conservation and whitelisted field changes.

Exact tested artifact/lock hashes and observed resource limits live in the review
receipts. Game execution, persistence and recovery are distinct checks and remain
`not_run` unless a receipt explicitly records them for the exact candidate.

files.NOTICE:
SaveRift Assassin's Creed Shadows connector

Original connector integration, typed operations and custom UI are Apache-2.0.
This package is an independent developer implementation, not an Ubisoft product.
No game binaries, player save bytes, credentials, official artwork or proprietary
catalog are included. Package-local identity strings are not Xbox title IDs.

The compiled runtime includes the public SaveRift SDK's portable hash and binary
helpers: Noble hashes (MIT), Buffer (MIT), base64-js (MIT), and ieee754
(BSD-3-Clause). The compiled UI includes React/React DOM (MIT). Full notices are
in licenses/. The isolated QuickJS runner is a separate SDK dependency, not
embedded in this connector. Its licenses accompany the full SDK distribution.

The included UI is limited to query/stage/review through the public bounded
bridge. Candidate validation and retrieval remain trusted-host operations.
files.README.md:
# Assassin’s Creed Shadows — SaveRift connector

Experimental PC inventory support through SaveRift's existing isolated runtime,
custom UI and revision-bound shared draft. No game installation or account
connection is required to inspect a prepared file. This package does not contain
private saves, an account key, a proprietary decoder, or a third-party item catalog.

## Supported journey

1. Build the source with Node 22+: `npm ci --prefix ecosystem --ignore-scripts`,
   `npm ci --prefix ecosystem/sdk --ignore-scripts`,
   `npm ci --prefix ecosystem/workbench --ignore-scripts`, then
   `node ecosystem/plugins/ac-shadows/scripts/build.mjs` from the repository root.
2. Set `SAVERIFT_WORKBENCH_DIR` to a private directory **outside this checkout**.
   Run `node ecosystem/workbench/local-server.mjs` and open
   `http://127.0.0.1:4174` in a browser. Create an Assassin’s Creed Shadows workspace.
3. Select a supported prepared PC `.save` as role `main` and its local private
   transform file as role `ac-key`. Select any additional save-set files as
   `sibling`. Alternatively select an extracted progression context as
   `progression`; this fallback returns a context, not an installable save.
4. Build/test the selected plugin, then open its custom preview. Search/select an
   existing inventory record. Eligible records expose item level or quantity.
   Save an edit to the shared draft; review its original and proposed values.
5. Use **Review changes** to hand the draft to SaveRift's trusted host. Prepare
   the candidate, wait for all required phases, and download artifacts from that
   exact passed job. The private `ac-key` is input-only and is never a candidate.

The initial catalog uses exact item settings/instance IDs. It does not invent
localized item names. Unsupported fields have no enabled edit controls.

## Preparing an existing PC save

Raw PC saves normally contain Oodle-compressed contexts. The isolated runner has
no Oodle decoder. The optional **local authoring** command below converts only
the already-extracted inventory context to native stored blocks and preserves
every other context. It never runs a DLL, downloads a codec, opens the game,
changes ownership, or writes into a live save directory.

```text
node ecosystem/plugins/ac-shadows/scripts/prepare-native.mjs \
  --input /private/original.save \
  --decoded /private/extraction/snapshot.offset40.candidate.bin \
  --contexts /private/extraction/contexts.json \
  --output-dir /private/new-prepared-directory
```

Use a fresh verified extraction from your authorized local tools. The command
requires the prior AC extraction manifest shape (context/block offsets, lengths,
plaintext hashes and output paths). It checks that the decoded container belongs
to the exact input file, verifies its checksums and extraction metadata, walks
the inventory tree, and creates the prepared save, `private-transform.ac-key`,
and a receipt. It refuses overwrites and files inside the source checkout.

This command does **not independently decode Oodle**; validate the preparation
with an external decompressor before relying on it. The private opt-in oracle
under `tests/ac-shadows-independent-oracle.py` does this for the existing AC
research environment. Stored blocks are a recognized native container branch;
**game load/save/reload/recovery of this connector's output has not been tested**.
Untouched compressed target contexts fail with `AC_OODLE_REQUIRED` rather than
silently producing a context mislabeled as a complete save.

## Development and review

```text
node --test ecosystem/plugins/ac-shadows/tests/*.test.mjs
node ecosystem/workbench/cli.mjs call saverift_template_list
node ecosystem/workbench/stdio.mjs
```

The CLI, MCP server and browser share the same private workbench directory.
`tests/ac-shadows-private-flow.mjs` and `tests/ac-shadows-cli-mcp.mjs` exercise
the public service, real isolated execution and result retrieval. Private paths
enter through environment-selected config files; real bytes are never public
fixtures. See repository `docs/ac-shadows-validation.md` for the evidence split.

Source-only release review uses the existing `saverift_release_prepare` tool.
No AC hosted enrollment, production default, registry promotion or publication
is implied by a local package build or candidate success.
